scope: Isolated Flo customer staging only; policy treatment, not deployment approval

exceptions.reason: Use CloudWatch Logs default at-rest encryption instead of additional customer-managed KMS keys. Keep seven-day retention and minimal operational fields; do not log OAuth tokens, cookies, credentials or repair payloads. This exception concerns key management, not permission to store plaintext logs.

Keep SSEEnabled true with AWS-managed key management instead of customer-managed keys. Authentication values additionally require application-level AES-256-GCM encryption. This exception does not waive encryption or customer ownership checks.

Do not back up or restore login/session state: a restore can resurrect consumed login state or undo logout. Recover with a new empty auth table and new encryption key, requiring fresh sign-in. CustomerLinks and CustomerRepairs retain seven-day PITR and require revocation/ownership/deletion reconciliation before restored data can serve traffic.
Synchronous API Gateway HTTP workflow with no asynchronous event sources; errors return to the caller. Re-review before introducing asynchronous invocation.

No private-network dependencies in this isolated staging flow. Use TLS for AWS and Amazon endpoints. Public landing/login routes do not authorize customer data: data routes require a valid opaque session and a trusted Amazon-identity-to-customer mapping. Re-review for private integrations or production network requirements.

requiredControls: LwaEnabled=false until real profile and hosted-flow verification
No public enrollment or customer-link-writing endpoint
Runtime read-only access to trusted customer links and repair projections
Strongly consistent authorization reads and conditional auth-state writes
Session expiry, provider revalidation and logout enforcement
AWS/service credentials never authorize customer data
AWS-managed/default at-rest encryption and application-encrypted authentication values
Seven-day customer-link and repair PITR with restore reconciliation
Positive fixed reserved concurrency and bounded API/database throughput
No asynchronous event sources or public Lambda Function URL
Raw Guard findings remain visible; no suppression metadata
reviewTriggers: Before production or real customer repair data
Change to identity, storage, logging, backup, invocation or network assumptions
Any new Guard failure or affected resource outside the listed scope
